name: bm-v1-stage1-modulus-remodelling
claim: A coarse-grained collagen IV network (two-bead rods, stochastic NC1/7S crosslinks, no excluded volume) run through the spec's stage-1 protocol — stretch, hold, then switch the chemistry on — yields a separable elastic modulus and remodelling (stress-relaxation) time on real LAMMPS.
experiment: Build N two-bead rods in a quasi-2D periodic slab; assemble a crosslinked network with fix bond/create (NC1 binds 1, 7S binds 3); equilibrate with the chemistry frozen; apply an equibiaxial in-plane strain (fix deform) with the chemistry frozen (elastic loading); hold and read the elastic plateau; then switch crosslink make/break on and read the viscous stress relaxation. Network stress is the bond-virial pressure only (no kinetic term), normalised by the initial volume — the spec flags the all-atom stress as a stage-1 error.
result: Re-run 2026-10-01 with the parameters corrected to the released code (3σ rod, crosslink k=6/r0=0.5, cutoffs 0.65/1.35, damp=0.1, Nevery=500, σ≈125 nm). The stress-strain ramp gives a very soft tangent modulus consistent with zero at this network size (~−0.5 to +0.5 LJ across seeds, ~±1 Pa at kT/σ³ ≈ 2.2 Pa), consistent with the paper's ≈0.03 Pa linear modulus, and the chemistry-on hold shows a stress change as crosslinks turn over. The remodelling time is noise- limited at this network size (flagged, not silently zeroed) — calibration is spec decision #10. NOTE: the modulus is small/noise-limited, not a clean value; the earlier "floppy because central-force" explanation is retired (see bm-v3). FAITHFUL ANGLES + DENSITY CALIBRATION (2026-10-02): with the released NC1 angles created during assembly (use_real_angles, bm-v4) AND the geometry set to the authors' dense initial config (areal density 3.0 rods/σ², 12σ-thick slab, read from Assembly/input/dataNucType9_dense), the stiff network separates BOTH readouts reproducibly — a measurable elastic modulus (E ≈ 3 LJ ≈ 6 Pa) AND a measurable remodelling time (τ ≈ 40–60 τ), as the real viscous stress relaxes while crosslinks break. At this density make+break and make-only AGREE (≈2.6 crosslinks/rod), so the value is well-defined, not saturation-dependent. This is the elastic/viscous separation the study set out to do. The absolute Pa still depends on the open energy-scale decision (spec #4); ~6 Pa uses kT/σ³ ≈ 2.2 Pa.

purpose.question: Can the clean-room collagen IV network separate an elastic modulus from a viscous remodelling time, as the paper's staged protocol does?
purpose.mechanism: A crosslinked semiflexible rod network stores elastic energy in stretched bonds under fast load (crosslinks frozen), and dissipates it over the crosslink turnover time when make/break is switched on.
purpose.expected_outcome: A finite, very soft elastic modulus and a stress-relaxation time set by the crosslink kinetics (MP), calibratable to the ≈20 h collagen IV lifetime.

key_assumptions: One protomer = one two-bead rod; junction flexibility folded into a finite intra-rod bond (dynamic junction angles omitted in v1-minimal).
No excluded volume — every pair coefficient is zero (spec #2: the released input scripts set eps=0).
Crosslink make/break locked at FactorMult = 0.66 (make/break ratio 1.52), as in the released input scripts.
Quasi-2D slab; rods lie in-plane; thickness/layer count deferred (spec #9).
Energy unit = kT, so stress unit = kT/a³ ≈ 2.5 Pa; absolute pascals not yet claimed (spec #4).

limitations: Cross-check (2026-10-01): the released code includes NC1/7S junction angles (bending: angle_coeff 1 = 4.0 @180°, plus 7S angles) and a 3σ rod (r0=3.0). This study's floppy ~0 modulus is an artifact of omitting those angles (bending_k=0) and using a 1σ rod; it does not represent the published model. See references/cross-check-vs-released-code.md.
Network is floppy (z ≤ 3 < 4): central-force crosslinks alone give ~zero modulus; rigidity needs junction bending / bundling (FP1).
τ below detection while floppy — the relaxable stress is small; a rigid network is needed to resolve it.
No dynamic junction angles; persistence length is only approximately represented (spec: LAMMPS puts l_p as soft angles at junctions) — the load-bearing v2 gap.
No excluded volume, so pore-size / bundling readouts are not yet physical (deferred).
Modulus reported in LJ units / as a ratio, not calibrated pascals (spec #4).
Parameters transcribed from the spec's sheet, not ported from the authors' input scripts; those scripts are now public (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.20719515) but not yet cross-checked against this build.

report.title: Stage 1 — collagen IV modulus & remodelling (clean-room v1)
report.verdict: The staged protocol runs on real LAMMPS with the parameters corrected to the released code (2026-10-01). The elastic modulus is small and consistent with zero at this network size (~±1 Pa across seeds), consistent with the published model's own ≈0.03 Pa linear modulus. The remodelling mechanism is correct (crosslinks hold at a make/break steady state, freeze under load, and decay under breakage-only), but the relaxation signal is below detection at v1 scale, so τ is not yet resolved. The earlier "floppy because central-force z < 4" explanation is retired: the released model carries junction angles and is soft anyway (see bm-v3). The softness is inherent to the published model (missing components, thin-sheet geometry, no pre-stress — spec decision #4), not a connectivity threshold.
report.main_insight: The network is very soft (consistent with the published ≈0.03 Pa), but not because it is a sub-isostatic central-force network — the released model has junction angles and is still soft. Reporting a modulus in pascals for the vertex coupling awaits the energy-scale decision and a larger, faithful run.
report.caveat: Parameters are transcribed from the spec rather than ported from the authors' input scripts (now public, Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.20719515, not yet cross- checked); τ is below detection at 200 rods; the modulus is reported in LJ units (energy scale open).

findings.statement: LAMMPS `fix bond/break` models only OVER-STRETCH breaking, not a force- independent off-rate — small Rmax dissolves the network, large Rmax saturates it. Replacing it with a controlled random-deletion off-rate gives a make/break steady state and crosslink turnover.

evidence.observed: crosslinks 45→401 (old, densifies) vs steady ~54 then decay 46→3 (off-rate)

findings.explanation: Breaking must be length-independent to be a controllable rate (spec: force-independent in v1).
findings.next_action: adopted in viva_lumenoid/collagen.py; guarded by a regression test

findings.statement: The v1 central-force network is below the 2D rigidity threshold (mean z ≤ 3 < 4), so its elastic modulus is statistically consistent with zero — matching the published ≈0.03 Pa.

evidence.observed: modulus −0.03 ± 0.06 LJ (95% CI, 6 seeds); mean z ≈ 1.2; z_max = 3

findings.explanation: Maxwell counting: NC1 beads reach z = 2, 7S beads z = 4, mean ≤ 3 < 4 → floppy regardless of crosslink density. Rigidity must come from bending / bundling.

findings.statement: The remodelling mechanism is now correct (stress decays as crosslinks break), but the relaxable stress is small in a floppy network, so τ is below detection at v1 scale.

evidence.observed: ensemble viscous decay ~0.29→0.25; s0 < 2·noise → τ unresolved

findings.next_action: resolve on a rigid (bending) network or a much larger ensemble

followup_proposals.title: Junction bending stiffness → a non-zero, calibratable modulus
followup_proposals.motivation: v1 is floppy (z < 4); the spec says persistence length enters as soft angles where rods join. Add junction bending and measure modulus vs bending stiffness to reach the rigid regime the vertex model needs.
followup_proposals.hypothesized_mechanism: Bending rigidity at crosslink junctions lifts the network above the floppy limit, giving a finite modulus even at z < 4.

followup_proposals.title: Off-rate → remodelling-time calibration to the ≈20 h collagen IV lifetime
followup_proposals.motivation: τ ≈ 1/off_rate is the knob the spec calibrates (decision #10). Sweep off_rate on a rigid network and map τ(off_rate) to ≈20 h to set the time unit.
followup_proposals.hypothesized_mechanism: τ scales as 1/off_rate; a rigid network makes it measurable.

resolved_uncertainties: The viscous 'relaxation' densification was a fix-bond/break artifact — root-caused and fixed.
The ~0 modulus is rigidity-percolation physics (z < 4), not a measurement failure.
remaining_uncertainties: τ (remodelling time) — below detection until the network is rigid.
Absolute modulus in pascals — energy scale still open (spec #4).

followup_study_proposals.title: Off-rate → τ calibration to the ≈20 h lifetime

regression_compatibility.basis: No upstream regression baseline for this clean-room build.

biological_validation.basis: Consistent with the published ≈0.03 Pa (near-floppy) modulus; the floppiness is mechanistically explained by connectivity (z < 4).

explanatory_gain.basis: Identifies WHY the BM network is soft — connectivity below rigidity percolation — telling the vertex model that BM stiffness comes from bending/bundling, not crosslink count.

expert_questions: Energy scale (spec decision #4): should the elastic modulus be reported in absolute pascals — by fitting the LJ energy unit to a measured BM modulus — or kept in reduced units / reported as the ratio s_E? Our faithful value is ~3 LJ (≈ 6 Pa at kT/σ³≈2.2 Pa); the published figure is ≈0.03 Pa under the authors' own s_E. Which convention should the AICS vertex-model coupling use?

Equilibrium crosslink fraction / GCE: the absolute modulus scales strongly with crosslink fraction (E≈0 at 0.72 crosslinks/rod → ≈8 Pa at 2.5/rod). Our make-only path saturates at ~2.6/rod, while the authors' GCE (Nucleation/Death) + distance-gated breaking sets a specific equilibrium fraction. What equilibrium crosslink fraction (or free-monomer concentration / off-rate) should we target to match the published network?
